title: seller-experiment-lab-18min-scripts-draft
executive_summary: Compact seller lab designed for technical sellers and SEs to run an 18-minute discovery + demo experiment that drives pilot commitments. Combines a tightly timed flow, two A/B script variants, an economics quick-check, and a minimal handoff template. Purpose is speed: get into a measurable pilot or put a next-step on the calendar within the call.
objectives: Confirm the single production constraint (latency or cost) that matters for the prospect
Demonstrate a fast-path Redwood configuration that solves the constraint in <10s of minutes
Elicit a pilot commitment (reserved capacity trial or short Dedicated proof) or put a technical follow-up on calendar
Capture quantitative baseline metrics for later ROI conversation
target_audience: technical seller + SE pair running live calls with integration architects, platform teams, or machine-learning engineers
lab_timing: 0-2m: Rapid hook + agenda (why this lab is 18m and what success looks like)
7-12m: Live demo and economics check on a real snippet or sample payload
12-16m: Pilot design and SLA sketch (what success looks like in a 2-week pilot)
16-18m: Commit to next steps and immediate handoff
play_flow: Intro hook: 30s value snapshot, name relevant constraint (latency/cost/privacy)
Discovery pivot: ask for exact SLA or token budgets and a 1-2 sentence current flow description
Demo pivot: run two quick variants (hosted low-latency vs dedicated predictable throughput) and show output + latency/econ numbers
Pilot sketch: propose a minimal pilot (3 endpoints, X tokens/day or Y reserved seconds), success metrics, rollback conditions
Handoff: send templated follow-up with contact, resources, and JIRA ticket created for pilot onboarding
discovery-script: Variant A opener: 'If we could cut your median inference latency by half without raising your monthly bill more than 10%, what would you do first?'
Variant B opener: 'Tell me the most painful failure mode in your current inference stack — is it throughput, cost spikes, or ops/personnel overhead?'
Follow-ups: 'What SLA do you promise downstream services?'; 'How many concurrent requests at peak?'; 'Any regulatory constraints on data motion?'
Redwood prompt: 'Do you prefer a predictable reserved capacity contract or an elastic hosted path for your initial pilot?'
demo-scripts: Live sample: 'We'll run your sample prompt (or our sanitized example) against two configs: a small-hosted variant tuned for latency and a dedicated provisioned pod tuned for throughput.'
Explain metrics: 'This right-hand column shows per-request median latency, this shows cost-per-1k tokens using our Optimize suggestion.'
Fallback demo: 'If capacity is constrained we can automatically route to a quantized variant with a configured quality guard — here's a live comparison.'
Ops note: 'Show Console trace for token breakdown and per-route cost — point to trace id for post-call review.'
objection-responses: Objection: 'We can't commit to reserved capacity yet.' || Response: 'We can run a 2-week mini-reserved trial with a shallow commit and an ops-runbook for automatic fallbacks — you get predictable throughput without long-term lock-in.'

Objection: 'I'm worried about quality regressions with quantized models.' || Response: 'We tie quality to prompt sets and run gated rollouts; we can show evaluation diffs and set a regression alert before any production traffic switches.'
Objection: 'Security/compliance is a must.' || Response: 'We can run the control plane in your VPC and integrate with your KMS/HSM; we'll include an audit trail for the pilot.'
canary-checklist: Define rollback condition: p95 latency > X or quality drop > Y%
Pin model versions and enable canary routing for 10% traffic
Set regression thresholds and enable alerts to SE + customer SRE
Confirm data residency and logging policy for pilot traces
Document contact and escalation path in the pilot ticket
handoff-templates: Email subject: Redwood pilot: config sketch + next steps
Email body: 'Thanks — attached is the pilot sketch (reserved 2-week trial). SE: <name>. Ops: onboarding runbook link. Next step: schedule kick-off (30m) and share sanitized sample payload.'
Ticket template: 'Pilot start date, reserved units, expected traffic pattern, rollback criteria, contacts (customer, SE, SRE), linked evaluation prompt set and traces.'
slide_titles: Hook: what we can try in 18 minutes
Two quick configs and what they buy you
Live run: numbers and quality snapshot
Pilot sketch: minimal scope + success metrics
notes_to_self: Keep the lab low-friction: always ask for a real sample or commit to use a sanitized sample and capture token counts. Two variants give the prospect a real choice; always surface both latency and unit-economics immediately. After the call, create JIRA pilot ticket and attach the Console trace id. Iterate scripts based on Region (APAC customers prefer early talk of Private deployment options).
